titre_chapitre: Production Cycles, Product Types, and Bills of Materials (BOM)

questions.enonce: Among the three production cycles defined in the generic model, which is the most important from the customer's and competition's point of view?
options: The production cycle (1)
The commercial cycle (2)
The financial cycle (3)
The procurement cycle
questions.explication: The commercial cycle (between order and delivery) is the only one the customer truly knows and uses to compare the company with its competitors[span_0](start_span)[span_0](end_span).

questions.enonce: What is the main distinction between a standard product and a specific product?
options: A standard product is manufactured for a single customer, while a specific product is intended for a broad audience without distinction.
A standard product is purchased by a large number of customers without distinction, while a specific product is made according to the wishes of a particular customer.
There is no difference, both notions are interchangeable.
A standard product necessarily incorporates repair services.
questions.explication: A standard product (like a laundry pack or a movie show) addresses a large audience without distinction, whereas a specific product (like a custom-made suit) meets the precise wishes of a customer[span_1](start_span)[span_1](end_span).

questions.enonce: Why does product complexity (e.g., a large number of components) increase manufacturing risks according to probabilistic analysis?
options: Because it automatically reduces purchasing costs.
Because multiplying high individual probabilities over thousands of components causes the overall probability of having all components available to drop.
Because it eliminates the need for purchasing bills of materials.
Because it guarantees a permanent availability of 100% of the parts.
questions.explication: Complexity introduces risks: for example, with 3,000 components each having a 99.99% availability probability, the overall probability of having all components available simultaneously is only 74%[span_2](start_span)[span_2](end_span).

questions.enonce: What is the main trade-off to manage regarding product variety or diversity (the product range)?
options: Variety is a tremendous competitive advantage, but it generates significant complexity and management risks that must be successfully controlled.
Variety must be completely banned to simplify the workshop.
Variety has no impact on the company's manufacturing processes.
Variety systematically reduces the number of possible combinations to a single one.
questions.explication: Offering many options is a highly appreciated competitive advantage, but it generates high complexity (as illustrated by the simple example of a pencil offering 1,120 possibilities)[span_3](start_span)[span_3](end_span).

questions.enonce: What is the rule for using negative coefficients (resulting from an extraction operation, for example) in bill of materials calculations?
options: They must be multiplied by the scrap rate in the purchasing bill of materials.
They have no impact and must not be taken into account when calculating quantities in the purchasing (procurement) bill of materials.
They serve to automatically increase finished goods inventory.
They completely replace the company's financial cycle.
questions.explication: When an extraction operation creates a negative coefficient in the manufacturing bill of materials, it has no incidence on the purchasing bill of materials, because the initial quantity of material still had to be purchased[span_4](start_span)[span_4](end_span).
